title: What Was the First Book Ever Written?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: using spoken words rather than writing
a flat object used for writing in ancient times, often made of clay or stone
normal written or spoken language that is not poetry
a long fictional book with characters and a developed story
connected to literature, books, or serious writing
the ability to read and write
to produce and distribute a book, article, or other written work

sentences.en: Humans have been speaking languages for tens of thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 人类使用语言已经有几万年了。

sentences.en: We told stories around fires, passed down myths from parents to children, and memorised important information about survival and history.
sentences.zh: 我们在火堆旁讲述故事，将神话代代相传，并记住了关于生存和历史的重要信息。

sentences.en: But for a very long time, nobody could write anything down.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，没有人能把任何东西写下来。

sentences.en: Then, at some point, humans invented writing.
sentences.zh: 后来，在某个时期，人类发明了文字。

sentences.en: Writing allowed people to record laws, preserve stories, collect knowledge, and communicate across generations.
sentences.zh: 文字让人类能够记录法律、保存故事、积累知识并跨越代际进行交流。

sentences.en: Eventually, writing gave us books. Today, I want to explore the history of books, from ancient clay tablets in Mesopotamia to modern audiobooks and e-books on smartphones.
sentences.zh: 最终，文字为我们带来了书籍。今天，我想探索书籍的历史，从美索不达米亚的古代泥板，到智能手机上的现代有声书和电子书。

sentences.en: We’ll look at the origins of writing, the oldest surviving texts, the first true “books,” the world’s first novels, the printing revolution, the bestselling books in history, and finally… the future of reading itself.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨文字的起源、现存最古老的文本、最早真正的“书”、世界上第一部小说、印刷革命、历史上最畅销的书籍，最后……阅读本身的未来。

sentences.en: And we will do all of this while learning some new vocabulary and practicing your English listening comprehension.
sentences.zh: 我们将在做这一切的同时，学习一些新词汇，并练习你的英语听力理解。

sentences.en: Before humans invented writing, our knowledge had to be passed down orally.
sentences.zh: 在人类发明文字之前，我们的知识必须通过口头传递。

sentences.en: This means using our voices. People communicated about their history or religion, laws and stories by speaking and listening rather than by reading books.
sentences.zh: 这意味着使用我们的声音。人们通过说和听，而不是通过读书，来交流他们的历史或宗教、法律和故事。

sentences.en: This is known as an oral tradition. There are still some cultures around the world that maintain the oral tradition.
sentences.zh: 这被称为口头传统。世界上仍有一些文化保持着口头传统。

sentences.en: It is famously a big part of Australian Aboriginal culture, as well as many other indigenous societies who never developed writing.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，这是澳大利亚原住民文化的重要组成部分，许多其他从未发展出文字的原住民社会也是如此。

sentences.en: Today, though, the vast majority of us rely on writing.
sentences.zh: 然而今天，我们绝大多数人都依赖文字。

sentences.en: Written information like books and websites, notes and messages.
sentences.zh: 文字信息，比如书籍和网站、便条和信息。

sentences.en: I think it’s actually difficult to imagine a society without writing.
sentences.zh: 我想实际上很难想象一个没有文字的社会。

sentences.en: Imagine your life if there was no writing at all in your world.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你的世界里完全没有文字，你的生活会是什么样。

sentences.en: But for most of human history, writing didn’t exist.
sentences.zh: 但在人类历史的大部分时间里，文字并不存在。

sentences.en: Modern humans have existed for about 300,000 years, I guess, but writing only developed around 5000 or 6000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想，现代人类已经存在了大约30万年，但文字是在大约5000或6000年前才发展起来的。

sentences.en: That means humans lived without written language for the vast majority of our existence.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人类在绝大多数生存时期里都没有书面语言。

sentences.en: Some historians believe that famous works like Homer’s Iliad and The Odyssey were actually oral stories before they were eventually written down years after they were first told.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，像荷马史诗《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》这样的名著，在最初被讲述多年后最终被写下来之前，实际上都是口头故事。

sentences.en: Professional storytellers may have remembered enormous amounts of material.
sentences.zh: 专业的故事讲述者可能记住了大量的素材。

sentences.en: So if humans were already able to communicate and keep their stories using their voices, why did we develop writing?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人类已经能够通过声音进行交流并保留他们的故事，我们为什么还要发展文字呢？

sentences.en: While I’d love to say the answer to that question was something creative or romantic, like recording our religious stories or some great events or writing amazing novels, the real answer is probably a bit boring.
sentences.zh: 虽然我很想说这个问题的答案是某种富有创造性或浪漫色彩的东西，比如记录我们的宗教故事、一些伟大的事件或撰写精彩的小说，但真正的答案可能有点无趣。

sentences.en: Writing most likely came from administration and accounting.
sentences.zh: 文字最有可能源于行政管理和会计。

sentences.en: Most historians believe the first culture to develop writing was the ancient Mesopotamians.
sentences.zh: 大多数历史学家认为，第一个发展出文字的文化是古代美索不达米亚人。

sentences.en: Mesopotamia was a region in the Middle East that includes modern-day Iraq.
sentences.zh: 美索不达米亚是中东的一个地区，包括现在的伊拉克。

sentences.en: Around 3400 to 3200 BCE, the Sumerians, who lived in Mesopotamia, created one of the earliest known writing systems… cuneiform.
sentences.zh: 在大约公元前3400年至3200年，生活在美索不达米亚的苏美尔人创造了最早已知文字系统之一……楔形文字。

sentences.en: Cuneiform symbols were pressed into soft clay tablets using a stylus, like a stick.
sentences.zh: 楔形文字符号是用触笔（类似于小棍子）压印在软泥板上的。

sentences.en: The symbols looked wedge-shaped, and because they wrote in clay, we still have a lot of these records remaining from the past.
sentences.zh: 这些符号看起来呈楔形，而且因为他们写在泥土上，我们至今仍保留着许多这样的古代记录。

sentences.en: Clay is quite good at surviving through the years.
sentences.zh: 泥土非常经久耐用。

sentences.en: The earliest examples of writing were practical records.
sentences.zh: 最早的文字范例是实用记录。

sentences.en: Ancient people used writing to track things like their taxes, trade, supplies, property.
sentences.zh: 古代人们用文字来追踪税收、贸易、物资、财产等事情。

sentences.en: It is in cuneiform writing from the Sumerians that we also have the earliest known name of a person: Kushim.
sentences.zh: 正是在苏美尔人的楔形文字中，我们还找到了最早已知的人名：库什姆（Kushim）。

sentences.en: According to a tablet from 5000 years ago, we know Kushim was responsible for the production and storage of barley, and he signed his name on his tablet.
sentences.zh: 根据一块5年前的泥板，我们知道库什姆负责大麦的生产和储存，他在自己的泥板上签了名。

sentences.en: Kushim used writing to record shipments into and out of his warehouse.
sentences.zh: 库什姆用文字记录进出他仓库的货物运输。

sentences.en: He also is famous for making the first ever accounting mistake, which I find hilarious.
sentences.zh: 他还因犯下了历史上第一个会计错误而闻名，我觉得这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: As cities grew larger, remembering everything orally became really difficult.
sentences.zh: 随着城市规模越来越大，靠口头记住所有事情变得非常困难。

sentences.en: Written records allow people to store their information more accurately.
sentences.zh: 文字记录使人们能够更准确地存储信息。

sentences.en: People who were trained to read and write were known as scribes, and scribes usually had quite an important position in society because writing was a special skill, and it was quite rare in some of these ancient places.
sentences.zh: 受过读写训练的人被称为书吏（scribes），书吏在社会中通常享有相当重要的地位，因为写作是一项特殊的技能，在其中一些古代地方相当罕见。

sentences.en: Writing systems also developed independently in other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 文字系统也在世界其他地区独立发展起来。

sentences.en: Ancient Egypt developed hieroglyphics, and other writing systems emerged in China and in Mesoamerica as well.
sentences.zh: 古埃及发展出了象形文字，其他文字系统也在中国和中美洲出现。

sentences.en: I think the fact that multiple civilizations invented writing independently is one of the most interesting things about this topic.
sentences.zh: 我认为多个文明独立发明文字这一事实是这个话题中最有趣的事情之一。

sentences.en: Very different societies eventually reached the same conclusion: speaking and listening was not enough to organize a complicated society.
sentences.zh: 截然不同的社会最终得出了相同的结论：仅仅靠说和听不足以组织一个复杂的社会。

sentences.en: And maybe some language learners could also do with this advice.
sentences.zh: 也许一些语言学习者也可以听取这个建议。

sentences.en: I know when I’m studying Japanese, I tend to focus on speaking and listening, and I tend to not practice my reading and writing as much as I should.
sentences.zh: 我知道当我在学习日语时，我倾向于专注于说和听，而往往没有像应有的那样去练习读和写。

sentences.en: Eventually, speaking and listening are not enough.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，说和听是不够的。

sentences.en: You also need to learn to read and write.
sentences.zh: 你还需要学习读和写。

sentences.en: So what are the oldest written books that we have ever discovered?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们发现的最古老的书面书籍是什么？

sentences.en: Well, as I’ve already mentioned, the earliest known examples of writing are those administrative clay tablets from Mesopotamia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我已经提到的，最早已知的文字例子是美索不达米亚的那些行政泥板。

sentences.en: These tablets date back more than 5000 years, but they weren’t really books.
sentences.zh: 这些泥板可以追溯到5000多年前，但它们并不真的是书。

sentences.en: They were tablets, used to record records and administrative texts.
sentences.zh: 它们是泥板，用于记录档案和行政文本。

sentences.en: If we want to think about the earliest literary works, historians usually point to a few different places.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想考虑最早的文学作品，历史学家通常会指向几个不同的地方。

sentences.en: One is the Instructions of Shuruppak, which is an ancient Sumerian text, and it contains advice and moral guidance.
sentences.zh: 一个是《舒如帕克箴言》（Instructions of Shuruppak），这是一部古苏美尔文本，包含建议和道德指导。

sentences.en: Another suggestion is the Egyptian Pyramid Texts, which are religious writings carved inside of pyramids to help the dead find their way to the afterlife But the most famous example of an early story is the Epic of Gilgamesh.
sentences.zh: 另一个建议是《埃及金字塔铭文》（Pyramid Texts），这是雕刻在金字塔内部的宗教文字，旨在帮助死者找到通往来世的路，但早期故事最著名的例子是《吉尔伽美什史诗》（Epic of Gilgamesh）。

sentences.en: Gilgamesh is often described as the oldest surviving great work of literature, and it is perhaps the first ever written story.
sentences.zh: 《吉尔伽美什》通常被描述为现存最古老的伟大文学作品，它也许是有史以来第一部被写下来的故事。

sentences.en: It originated in Mesopotamia thousands of years ago and follows King Gilgamesh on a journey searching for immortality after the death of his friend.
sentences.zh: 它几千年前起源于美索不达米亚，讲述了吉尔伽美什国王在朋友死后踏上寻求永生之旅的故事。

sentences.en: Even though it was written over 4,000 years ago, quite a few of the themes in the story are still recognizable today.
sentences.zh: 尽管它写于4000多年前，但故事中的相当一部分主题在今天依然能引起共鸣。

sentences.en: People in the ancient world obviously worried about many of the same things that we worry about now.
sentences.zh: 古代世界的人们显然担心着许多和我们现在担心的事情一样的事情。

sentences.en: But was Gilgamesh the first book ever written?
sentences.zh: 但《吉尔伽美什》是第一本被写出来的书吗？

sentences.en: Well, the problem is that ancient people did not use books in the modern sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题在于古代人并不以现代意义上的方式使用书籍。

sentences.en: When we think of a book today, we usually imagine pages bound together with a cover.
sentences.zh: 今天当我们想到一本书时，我们通常会想象用封面装订在一起的书页。

sentences.en: But humans used many different formats for storing written information before books were invented.
sentences.zh: 但在书籍发明之前，人类使用许多不同的格式来存储书面信息。

sentences.en: Sumerians used clay tablets. Ancient Egyptians used scrolls made from papyrus.
sentences.zh: 苏美尔人使用泥板。古埃及人使用由纸莎草制成的卷轴。

sentences.en: The oldest Chinese writing examples were carved into animal bones and turtle shells.
sentences.zh: 最古老的中国文字例子是被刻在动物骨头和乌龟壳上的。

sentences.en: Are these books? I guess the predecessor to the modern book is the codex.
sentences.zh: 这些是书吗？我猜现代书籍的前身是手抄本（codex）。

sentences.en: A codex is a series of handwritten pages of text which are then stacked on top of each other and bound along one side.
sentences.zh: 手抄本是一系列手写的文字页，然后将它们叠放在一起，沿着一边装订。

sentences.en: The codex became popular during the Roman period in Europe.
sentences.zh: 手抄本在欧洲的罗马时期变得流行。

sentences.en: The oldest surviving codices (which is the plural of codex) tend to be religious texts.
sentences.zh: 现存最古老的手抄本（codices是codex的复数）往往是宗教文本。

sentences.en: Of course, there would’ve probably been some more written in the past, but the ones that we have today, the ones that have been best preserved, are typically religious.
sentences.zh: 当然，过去可能还写过更多，但我们今天拥有的、保存最完好的那些，通常都是宗教文本。

sentences.en: Some of the most interesting codices were found in the Nag Hammadi Library.
sentences.zh: 一些最有趣的手抄本是在纳格·哈马迪图书馆（Nag Hammadi Library）中发现的。

sentences.en: The Nag Hammadi Library was discovered in Egypt in 1945 and contains Christian texts from around 1,600 years ago.
sentences.zh: 纳格·哈马迪图书馆于1945年在埃及被发现，里面藏有大约1600年前的基督教文献。

sentences.en: But interestingly, they contained early Christian texts known as Gnostic texts, which are very different from modern Christianity.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，它们包含被称为诺斯替教文本（Gnostic texts）的早期基督教文献，这与现代基督教非常不同。

sentences.en: They were written in a period before Christians had decided exactly what to believe, exactly what their religion was going to focus on.
sentences.zh: 它们写于基督徒决定究竟应该相信什么、他们的宗教到底要关注什么之前的时期。

sentences.en: Are these books? Well, they were written texts bound together.
sentences.zh: 这些是书吗？嗯，它们是装订在一起的书面文本。

sentences.en: But I don’t think we would consider them to be a book in the way that we understand books.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们不会把它们当作我们所理解的书。

sentences.en: Same as the early scrolls and tablets we have from the Middle East and parts of Asia, they’re definitely writing.
sentences.zh: 就像我们从中东和亚洲部分地区获得的早期卷轴和泥板一样，它们绝对是文字。

sentences.en: They’re definitely examples of writing, but are they books?
sentences.zh: 它们绝对是写作的例子，但它们是书吗？

sentences.en: It’s more debatable. So far, I’ve talked about the origins of writing and some of the oldest texts in history.
sentences.zh: 这更有争议。到目前为止，我讨论了文字的起源和历史上一些最古老的文本。

sentences.en: But when I think of a book, to tell you the truth, I’m imagining a novel.
sentences.zh: 但当我想象一本书时，说实话，我脑海里浮现的是一部小说。

sentences.en: That’s just my perspective. So I thought it would be interesting to think about the first ever novel.
sentences.zh: 这只是我的看法。所以我认为思考有史以来第一部小说会很有趣。

sentences.en: A novel is a long fictional prose narrative with developed characters and a complex story.
sentences.zh: 小说是一部具有成熟人物和复杂情节的长篇虚构散文叙事。

sentences.en: Prose is normal everyday language that follows normal grammar rules.
sentences.zh: 散文是遵循普通语法规则的日常普通语言。

sentences.en: A lot of early writing was not in prose, but it was written as poetry.
sentences.zh: 许多早期的写作不是散文，而是以诗歌形式写成的。

sentences.en: Epics like Homer’s Odyssey or Beowulf or the Epic of Gilgamesh were technically poems.
sentences.zh: 像荷马的《奥德赛》、埃乌尔夫（Beowulf）或《吉尔伽美什史诗》这样的史诗严格来说都是诗歌。

sentences.en: They weren’t prose. They weren’t what we’d consider a normal story.
sentences.zh: 它们不是散文。它们不是我们认为的普通故事。

sentences.en: One of the strongest candidates for the world’s first true novel is The Tale of Genji, written in 11th century Japan by Murasaki Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 世界上第一部真正小说最有力的候选者之一是《源氏物语》（The Tale of Genji），由紫式部（Murasaki Shikibu）于11世纪在日本写成。

sentences.en: She was a lady-in-waiting, so a servant, for the Empress of Japan at the time.
sentences.zh: 她当时是日本皇后的一名内侍，也就是女官。

sentences.en: The novel was written during Japan’s Heian period, which was a time when aristocratic courts and that kind of culture flourished in Japan.
sentences.zh: 这部小说写于日本的平安时代，当时贵族宫廷和这种文化在日本蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: The Tale of Genji follows the life and relationships of Hikaru Genji, a nobleman living in the Imperial court.
sentences.zh: 《源氏物语》讲述了生活在帝国宫廷中的贵族光源氏（Hikaru Genji）的生活和人际关系。

sentences.en: This novel spends a lot of time talking about emotions and relationships, jealousy, romance, the inner lives of characters.
sentences.zh: 这部小说花了很多时间讨论情感和人际关系、嫉妒、浪漫以及人物的内心世界。

sentences.en: And this focus on characters is why it’s often considered the earliest thing to resemble a modern novel, because it’s more psychological.
sentences.zh: 这种对人物的关注就是它经常被认为是最早类似于现代小说的原因，因为它更具心理描写性。

sentences.en: It’s not just a basic story. It talks about people.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是一个简单的故事。它探讨的是人。

sentences.en: I’ve read The Tale of Genji. There are lots of translations out there if you’re interested in checking it out.
sentences.zh: 我读过《源氏物语》。如果你有兴趣了解它，有很多翻译版本可供选择。

sentences.en: I would recommend it. Of course, not everyone agrees.
sentences.zh: 我会推荐它。当然，并非所有人都同意。

sentences.en: Some people argue that later European works fit the definition of a novel more clearly.
sentences.zh: 一些人认为后来的欧洲作品更清楚地符合小说的定义。

sentences.en: Don Quixote, for example, was written by Miguel de Cervantes in the early 17th century.
sentences.zh: 例如，《堂吉诃德》（Don Quixote）是由米格尔·德·塞万提斯（Miguel de Cervantes）在17世纪初写成的。

sentences.en: Don Quixote tells the story of a man who becomes obsessed with medieval knight stories and begins confusing fiction with reality.
sentences.zh: 《堂吉诃德》讲述了一个痴迷于中世纪骑士故事并开始将虚构与现实混淆的男人的故事。

sentences.en: Other people point further back. They talk about ancient Greek and Roman prose fiction, which we do have lots of examples of, but were they really novels?
sentences.zh: 其他人则把时间推得更早。他们谈论古希腊和古罗马的散文小说，我们确实有很多这样的例子，但它们真的是小说吗？

sentences.en: We can’t talk about the history of books without talking about printing.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论书籍的历史，就不能不谈论印刷术。

sentences.en: The earliest large-scale printing technology developed in China centuries before Europe.
sentences.zh: 中国在欧洲几个世纪前就发展出了最早的大规模印刷技术。

sentences.en: One common method was woodblock printing, where entire pages of text were carved into wooden blocks, covered with ink, and pressed onto paper.
sentences.zh: 常见的一种方法是雕版印刷，即把整页文字雕刻在木板上，涂上墨水，然后压印到纸上。

sentences.en: This allowed text to be copied much faster than writing everything by hand.
sentences.zh: 这使得文字复制的速度比全靠手抄快得多。

sentences.en: One very famous example is the Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist text printed in 868 CE.
sentences.zh: 一个非常著名的例子就是《金刚经》，这是一部在公元868年印刷的佛教经典。

sentences.en: It is considered the oldest known printed book in the world.
sentences.zh: 它被认为是世界上已知最古老的印刷书。

sentences.en: Around the 1450s, Johannes Gutenberg developed the movable type printing press.
sentences.zh: 大约在1450年前后，约翰内斯·古腾堡发明了活字印刷机。

sentences.en: Instead of carving entire pages into wood, printers could arrange individual metal letters and then reuse them repeatedly for different pages.
sentences.zh: 印刷工人们不用再把整页文字雕刻在木头上，而是可以排列单个金属活字，并在不同的页面上重复使用。

sentences.en: This made printing dramatically faster and so much more efficient.
sentences.zh: 这让印刷速度大幅提升，效率也高得多。

sentences.en: The Gutenberg Bible became one of the earliest major books printed in Europe using this type of printing press.
sentences.zh: 《古腾堡圣经》成为欧洲最早使用这种印刷机批量印刷的重要书籍之一。

sentences.en: Before printing, books had to be copied by hand.
sentences.zh: 在印刷术出现之前，书籍只能靠手抄。

sentences.en: Making a single book could take months, which made books really expensive and quite rare.
sentences.zh: 制作一本书可能需要几个月的时间，这让书籍变得极其昂贵且相当稀少。

sentences.en: Printing changed everything. Books became cheaper.
sentences.zh: 印刷术改变了一切。书籍变得便宜了。

sentences.en: They were much faster to make and more accessible.
sentences.zh: 它们的制作速度快得多，也更容易获取了。

sentences.en: Literacy rates gradually increased as well.
sentences.zh: 识字率也随之逐渐提高。

sentences.en: More people had access to written materials, which meant more people were able to read.
sentences.zh: 更多的人能够接触到文字资料，这意味着更多的人能够读书。

sentences.en: Because more people were able to read, scientific ideas could spread across countries.
sentences.zh: 因为更多的人能够读书，科学思想得以在各个国家传播开来。

sentences.en: Newspapers emerged. The education systems of countries grew and expanded.
sentences.zh: 报纸涌现了。各国的教育体系也随之成长和扩张。

sentences.en: Some historians argue that the printing press helped make things like the Protestant Reformation and the scientific revolution possible.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，印刷机促成了宗教改革和科学革命等重大历史事件的发生。

sentences.en: When I was a history student many years ago, my university considered the invention of the printing press the start of a new period of history, the early modern period.
sentences.zh: 许多年前，当我还是个历史系学生时，我的大学将印刷术的发明视为一个新历史时期——早期现代史的开端。

sentences.en: For a long time, the world’s most widely distributed books were religious texts like the Bible, the Quran, or Buddhist texts.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，世界上发行最广的书籍都是像《圣经》、《古兰经》或佛教经典这样的宗教典籍。

sentences.en: These were copied and then spread across the world.
sentences.zh: 这些书籍被抄写并传播到世界各地。

sentences.en: But over time, books also became forms of entertainment, especially during the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，书籍也变成了娱乐形式，尤其是在18和19世纪。

sentences.en: The fact that more people could read and printing technology was getting better meant there were just more people willing to buy books and read stories.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人能够识字，印刷技术也在不断进步，这意味着有更多的人愿意买书和读故事了。

sentences.en: Novels became particularly popular in a form called serialized novels.
sentences.zh: 小说变得格外流行，出现了一种叫做连载小说的形式。

sentences.en: Instead of publishing the entire book at once, writers would release their story chapter by chapter in newspapers or magazines.
sentences.zh: 作家们不会一下子出版整本书，而是会在报纸或杂志上一章一章地发表他们的故事。

sentences.en: Readers would then wait for the next installment.
sentences.zh: 读者们则会等待下一期的更新。

sentences.en: Cheap stories known as “penny dreadfuls “became really popular in Britain, and characters from these stories, like Sherlock Holmes, have now become internationally famous.
sentences.zh: 被称为“一分钱惊悚小说”的廉价故事在英国大受欢迎，而这些故事里的角色，比如Sherlock Holmes，如今已经闻名世界。

sentences.en: Sherlock Holmes’s original stories were published weekly or monthly, I think, in newspapers and magazines.
sentences.zh: 我想Sherlock Holmes最初的故事就是每周或每月在报纸和杂志上发表的。

sentences.en: While researching this episode, I became quite interested to find out what is the best-selling or the most distributed book in history.
sentences.zh: 在研究这一期节目时，我开始对弄清楚历史上最畅销或发行量最大的书是什么产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: For older books, especially, exact sale numbers are almost impossible to calculate.
sentences.zh: 对于年代较久远的书籍，精确的销售数字几乎是无法统计的。

sentences.en: Some books were copied and distributed for years before any records exist.
sentences.zh: 有些书籍在任何记录出现之前就已经被抄写并流传了多年。

sentences.en: And other books are spread religiously, maybe through churches or mosques, and maybe were not sold.
sentences.zh: 还有些书籍是通过宗教途径传播的，也许是通过教堂或清真寺，而且可能并不是拿来卖的。

sentences.en: The Christian Bible is often considered the most distributed or the best-selling book in history.
sentences.zh: 基督教的《圣经》通常被认为是历史上发行量最大或最畅销的书籍。

sentences.en: It has been translated into hundreds of languages and sent around the world for centuries.
sentences.zh: 它已经被翻译成了数百种语言，几个世纪以来被分发到世界各地。

sentences.en: Estimates vary, but billions of copies are believed to exist.
sentences.zh: 虽然估计数据各不相同，但人们认为现存的《圣经》有数十亿册。

sentences.en: The Quran, similarly, has been spread around the world and is considered the second-most distributed book in history, with also over a billion published.
sentences.zh: 同样，《古兰经》也在世界各地流传，被认为是历史上发行量第二大的书，发行量也超过了十亿册。

sentences.en: The third best-selling book in history, might surprise you.
sentences.zh: 历史上第三畅销的书可能会让你感到意外。

sentences.en: It is probably Quotations from Chairman Mao or The Little Red Book.
sentences.zh: 它很可能是《毛主席语录》或称《小红书》。

sentences.en: During the Cultural Revolution in China, enormous numbers of copies of this book were sent across the country for political and ideological reasons.
sentences.zh: 在中国文化大革命期间，出于政治和意识形态的原因，数量惊人的这本书被发送到了全国各地。

sentences.en: However, the Bible, the Quran, and Quotations from Chairman Mao are not really commercial bestsellers.
sentences.zh: 然而，《圣经》、《古兰经》和《毛主席语录》并非真正意义上的商业畅销书。

sentences.en: People read those books because of their importance, because of their religious or political significance.
sentences.zh: 人们阅读这些书是因为它们的重要性，是因为它们具有宗教或政治意义。

sentences.en: The best-selling or most widely read novels of all time include Don Quixote, which we mentioned earlier as maybe the first possible modern novel.
sentences.zh: 有史以来最畅销或被阅读最广泛的小说包括《堂吉诃德》（我们刚才提到它可能是第一部现代小说），

sentences.en: Also, A Tale of Two Cities by Charles Dickens, The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R.
sentences.zh: 还有查尔斯·狄更斯的《双城记》、J.R.R.

sentences.en: Tolkien, The Little Prince by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, and also Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone by J.K.
sentences.zh: 托尔金的《魔戒》、安东尼·德·圣埃克苏佩里的《小王子》，以及J.K.

sentences.en: Rowling. The Harry Potter series, all seven novels, are the best-selling book series in history.
sentences.zh: 罗琳的《哈利·波特与魔法石》。《哈利·波特》系列的所有七部小说是历史上最畅销的书籍系列。

sentences.en: One reason these books became so successful is translation.
sentences.zh: 这些书之所以能取得如此巨大的成功，原因之一就是翻译。

sentences.en: A book written in only one language has limited reach.
sentences.zh: 一本只用一种语言写成的书，其影响力是有限的。

sentences.en: But once books are translated into dozens or hundreds of languages, they can spread globally.
sentences.zh: 但一旦书籍被翻译成几十种或上百种语言，它们就能在全球范围内传播。

sentences.en: English language books also tend to dominate publishing.
sentences.zh: 英语图书在出版界也往往占据主导地位。

sentences.en: This is partly because of the historical influence of the United Kingdom and the United States.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为英国和美国在历史上的影响力。

sentences.en: English is the international language of business, science, entertainment, and education.
sentences.zh: 英语是商业、科学、娱乐和教育领域的国际语言。

sentences.en: Also, successful English language books are often turned into Hollywood movies or TV series, which then again increases their international popularity.
sentences.zh: 此外，成功的英文书籍通常会被改编成好莱坞电影或电视剧，这再次提升了它们在国际上的知名度。

sentences.en: How many people out there read the Harry Potter books after the success of the first Harry Potter movie?
sentences.zh: 有多少人在第一部哈利·波特电影大获成功之后去读了《Harry Potter》的书？

sentences.en: And how many read the books before the first Harry Potter movie?
sentences.zh: 又有多少人在第一部哈利·波特电影上映之前就读过这些书了呢？

sentences.en: Many incredibly important books were written in languages like Japanese, Arabic, Chinese, Spanish, Russian, and they will never achieve the same visibility as English language works, which is a big shame.
sentences.zh: 许多极其重要的著作是用日语、阿拉伯语、汉语、西班牙语、俄语等语言写成的，它们永远无法获得与英语作品相同的曝光度，这非常遗憾。

sentences.en: Let’s end this episode by thinking about the future of books.
sentences.zh: 让我们通过思考书籍的未来来结束这一集。

sentences.en: Books have already changed a lot throughout history.
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，书籍已经发生了很大的变化。

sentences.en: We have moved from clay tablets and scrolls to manuscripts, handwritten manuscripts, and now printed books.
sentences.zh: 我们已经从泥板和卷轴过渡到手稿、手抄本，再到现在的印刷书籍。

sentences.en: But actually, we are moving towards digital reading and e-books.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们正在走向数字阅读和电子书。

sentences.en: Things like the Amazon Kindle have changed how we read.
sentences.zh: 像 Amazon Kindle 这样的设备改变了我们的阅读方式。

sentences.en: Instead of carrying a physical book, you can store your entire library on a small electronic device.
sentences.zh: 你不再需要携带实体书，而是可以将整个图书馆储存在一个小型的电子设备上。

sentences.en: Also, in the past, you usually needed publishing companies to print and distribute your book if you wanted to write a book.
sentences.zh: 而且，在过去，如果你想写书，通常需要出版公司来印刷和发行你的书。

sentences.en: But now self-publishing is a massive industry.
sentences.zh: 但现在自主出版已经是一个庞大的产业。

sentences.en: You can publish books online, onto Kindle for example, without needing a publisher.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上出版书籍，比如发布到 Kindle 上，而不需要出版商。

sentences.en: You do it yourself, and you can become successful doing this.
sentences.zh: 你自己动手，并且可以通过这种方式获得成功。

sentences.en: Some famous examples of self-published books include The Martian by Andy Weir and Fifty Shades of Grey by E.L.
sentences.zh: 一些自主出版书籍的著名例子包括 Andy Weir 的《The Martian》和 E.L. James 的《Fifty Shades of Grey》。

sentences.en: James. Both of these became massive bestsellers, were turned into successful Hollywood movies, and were first published digitally without major support.
sentences.zh: 这两本书都成为了巨大的畅销书，被改编成了成功的好莱坞电影，而且最初都是在没有大型支持的情况下以数字方式出版的。

sentences.en: Audiobooks have also grown in popularity.
sentences.zh: 有声书的受欢迎程度也有所增长。

sentences.en: Recorded books have existed for decades, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，录音书籍已经存在了几十年。

sentences.en: But smartphones and streaming apps make audiobooks much more convenient.
sentences.zh: 但智能手机和流媒体应用让有声书变得更加方便。

sentences.en: You can now listen to them anywhere without needing to carry around a CD player or a cassette player.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以在任何地方收听它们，而不需要随身携带 CD 播放器或磁带播放器。

sentences.en: I used to listen to the Harry Potter books on cassette when I was seven or eight years old.
sentences.zh: 我七八岁的时候经常用磁带听《Harry Potter》。

sentences.en: The future may bring even bigger changes to writing and to books.
sentences.zh: 未来可能会给写作和书籍带来更大的改变。

sentences.en: I think we might see new ways of telling stories.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可能会看到讲故事的新方式。

sentences.en: Maybe interactive fiction that changes based on decisions in the book.
sentences.zh: 也许是根据书中的决定而改变的互动小说。

sentences.en: So you might be reading on your Kindle, and it gets to a point where the character can either agree to go swimming with a character or reject that character.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能正在用 Kindle 阅读，然后到了一个情节，主角可以同意和一个角色去游泳或者拒绝那个角色。

sentences.en: And depending on that decision, which way you choose, you get a different story.
sentences.zh: 根据那个决定，也就是你选择的方向，你会得到不同的故事。

sentences.en: These already exist in some form, but it might be more convenient digitally.
sentences.zh: 这些东西以某种形式已经存在了，但在数字设备上可能会更方便。

sentences.en: We might also see virtual reality storytelling.
sentences.zh: 我们可能还会看到虚拟现实叙事。

sentences.en: Some people worry about the future of reading.
sentences.zh: 有些人对阅读的未来感到担忧。

sentences.en: Some people worry that our attention spans are becoming shorter and reading is less common.
sentences.zh: 有些人担心我们的注意力正变得越来越短暂，阅读也变得不那么普遍了。

sentences.en: But this has been a similar fear for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但很长一段时间以来，这种担忧一直存在。

sentences.en: Television was supposed to destroy reading.
sentences.zh: 电视本该摧毁阅读。

sentences.en: The internet was supposed to destroy books.
sentences.zh: 互联网本该摧毁书籍。

sentences.en: But books have survived every shift so far.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，书籍在每一次变革中都生存了下来。

sentences.en: What was the first book ever written? I don’t think there’s a perfect answer.
sentences.zh: 历史上写成的第一本书是什么？我认为没有一个完美的答案。

sentences.en: If we mean the first written text, then the answer is probably some clay tablet created by the Sumerians 5,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 如果我们指的是最早的书面文本，那答案很可能是苏美尔人在 5,000 年前制作的一些泥板。

sentences.en: But they were just records and accounting documents.
sentences.zh: 但它们只是记录和财务会计文件。

sentences.en: If we mean the first great literary work, then maybe the Epic of Gilgamesh.
sentences.zh: 如果我们指的是第一部伟大的文学作品，那也许是《Epic of Gilgamesh》。

sentences.en: It’s the oldest surviving story that feels like a story.
sentences.zh: 它是现存最古老的、感觉像是一个故事的故事。

sentences.en: If we we mean something closer to a modern novel, then The Tale of Genji may deserve the title.
sentences.zh: 如果我们指的是更接近现代小说的作品，那么《The Tale of Genji》或许配得上这个称号。

sentences.en: Or the first mass-produced printed book, I guess that could be the Gutenberg Bible.
sentences.zh: 或者第一本大规模印刷的图书，我猜那可能是《Gutenberg Bible》。

sentences.en: Books have changed a lot throughout history, but I think we, we humans, have always had this love of storytelling.
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，书籍发生了很大的变化，但我认为我们人类一直都对讲故事充满热爱。

sentences.en: So hopefully the future of books is positive.
sentences.zh: 所以希望书籍的未来是光明的。

sentences.en: But what do you think? In your opinion, what would you say is the oldest book in history?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？在你看来，你认为历史最悠久的书是什么？

sentences.en: Actually, what counts as a book in your opinion?
sentences.zh: 实际上，在你看来，什么才算是一本书？

sentences.en: Does an ancient poem count as a book? Does it need to be printed in a modern way, or can a book be handwritten?
sentences.zh: 一首古代的诗算是一本书吗？它需要以现代的方式印刷吗，还是说手写的也可以是一本书？

sentences.en: Is reading an e-book just as good as reading a real book?
sentences.zh: 读电子书和读真正的书一样好吗？

sentences.en: And in 1,000 years, will people still read books at all?
sentences.zh: 在 1,000 年后，人们还会不会读书呢？
